review.note: M55: this record said 1530 to 1877 and both ends were file boundaries. Its interval is now Wikidata’s Q27306, P571 1701-01-18 and P576 1918-11-09. The ground it held before 1701 went to `brandenburg-prussia`, and the period that spanned the date is cut at it, outline unchanged. No succession is written to the German Empire: the two stand together for forty-seven years and end on the same day, which is not what `succeeded` says. See docs/m55-germany.md.

summary: A polity Historical Basemaps draws in the snapshots for 1530, 1600, 1650, 1700, 1715, 1783, 1800 and 1815 under the name "Prussia". That dataset is a set of world border snapshots from antiquity to the twentieth century; it is its authors’ work in progress and asks to be checked against other sources before use, and the span those snapshots cover — 1530 to 1877 — was this record’s interval until M55. It is now the Kingdom of Prussia’s own: Wikidata states P571 1701-01-18 and P576 1918-11-09 on Q27306, and neither of the old numbers was a claim about a polity beginning or ending. The snapshots before 1701 are `brandenburg-prussia`’s, and the one that begins in 1700 is cut at the kingdom’s inception. The kingdom outlives the German Empire’s founding by forty-seven years and ends on the same day as it, which is why no succession runs between them.
